A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MemoryCode study. Their text, figures, tables, and appendices A-H are readable and can be matched across pagination changes, supporting a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of five LLMs, including benchmark scores, instruction-update analyses, and RAG experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of eight LLMs, retains the appendix experiments, and provides a revised instruction-update analysis.

M1.justification: The core benchmark construction and scoring procedures remain unchanged: manually defined seeds, Command R+ dialogue generation, and regex-based instruction checks. Added evaluated models do not constitute changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic Python-coding benchmark with 360 histories, 51 instructions, and 80 fillers. The compositional-rule scenarios discussed in v2 Section 6.4 are proposed extensions, not additional evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Section 4.1, Figures 3-4, and Table 4 add Command A, DeepSeek-V3, and DeepSeek-R1 to the original five models, substantially expanding the comparison and introducing a reasoning model. Figure 6 separately narrows its model coverage from five models to GPT-4o.

E3.justification: Section 6.3 changes one analysis from grouping results by update rank without controlling session count to evaluating GPT-4o within fixed session counts. Figure 6 displays 30-, 40-, 50-, and 100-session groups. The main benchmark settings, scoring rules, and documented temperatures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The instruction-update analysis in Section 6.3 and Figure 6 is substantially revised to separate update count from session count. This directly reexamines whether repeated updates explain failure. The instruction-chain, RAG, instruction-difficulty, and illustrative error analyses are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Table 4 switches from standard deviations to standard errors. Captions for Figures 3, 8, and 9 explicitly identify 95% confidence intervals; Figures 8-9 already contained the same error bars in v1. No additional runs, seeds, or repeated-run protocol are established.

E6.justification: Added results change the leading models: v1's long-history leader was GPT-4o at 0.30, while v2 reports DeepSeek-R1 at 41.3% versus GPT-4o at 30.5%. DeepSeek-V3 achieves 100.0% on Instruction and 95.9% on Session. The revised Figure 6 replaces declining update-rank trends with approximately stable trends conditional on session count.

T1.justification: The update-rank definition and benchmark scoring logic are retained. Neither version adds or revises mathematical propositions, proofs, or formal derivations; the new session-count control is an empirical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract extends the degradation claim explicitly to DeepSeek-R1. The conclusion broadens its argument against scaling alone from model and context size to include dataset size and test-time compute. The central benchmark contribution and long-interaction failure claim remain.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 reverses an important interpretation: v1 attributes declining performance to difficulty incrementally updating instructions, whereas v2 emphasizes jointly following multiple rules after controlling session count. Section 6.4 also discusses untested compositional rule interactions. The dedicated Limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: The first-page code/data access pointer changes from for-ai/MemoryCode to Cohere-Labs-Community/MemoryCode. Appendix information on temperatures, retrieval settings, prompts, and computational costs is retained; the PDFs do not establish a change in resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Command A, DeepSeek-V3, and DeepSeek-R1. Section 2.2 adds an explicit distinction from MMMT-IF based on generation from scratch and evolving conversational instructions. The broader related-work organization and positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: There are targeted revisions to the abstract, model/results discussion, Sections 6.2-6.4, and conclusion, including renaming Section 6.2 to emphasize multi-instruction following. Affiliations and acknowledgments also change. The overall section and appendix structure is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 3 becomes full-width, Figures 3-4 accommodate additional models, and Figure 6 is redrawn with session-count series. Table 4 gains rows and revised ordering, percentage formatting, and uncertainty notation. Most other figures and tables retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The revised Section 6.3 addresses a confound in v1's explanation of update failures, and the expanded comparison provides direct evidence about a reasoning model. These strengthen the empirical account. The gains are qualified by the control being reported only for GPT-4o and the broader conclusion about dataset and test-time scaling lacking corresponding controlled experiments.
